title: fix(rootless): preserve systemd socket activation fds on re-exec
body:
When podman.service is socket-activated at user login it races with the other podman units to set up the rootless pause process.  If the re-executed child loses the race for the pause PID file, podman falls back to reexec_userns_join(), which forks again.

The parent of reexec_in_user_namespace() used to close the LISTEN_FDS socket (fd 3) before this fallback, so the final child inherited a stale fd 3 (the CLOEXEC user-namespace handle) and the journald datagram socket then reused fd 3.  The API service tried to accept(2) on a datagram socket and failed with "accept4: operation not supported", leaving podman.service failed at boot while a manual restart worked.

Stop closing the activation fds in the parent; they are released when the parent exits after the child terminates.

Log: Preserve systemd socket activation fds across the rootless re-exec

Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29964

Influence:
1. Reboot and verify podman.service reaches the active state
2. Verify podman.service survives concurrent startup with podman-restart, podman-auto-update and podman-clean-transient units
3. Verify socket-activated API requests over podman.sock still succeed
4. Verify manual "systemctl --user restart podman.service" still works
5. Verify the re-exec parent process does not leak file descriptors
6. Verify rootless container networking (rootlessport) is unaffected
